Design scope

What the architecture covers

Plan a family home with room for guests, everyday life and outdoor space. We balance public and private areas before the elevation takes shape.

01Public and private zonesKeep formal entertaining separate from daily family life.
02Kitchen planningPosition the kitchen, dirty kitchen and utility areas around real routines.
03Outdoor connectionUse terraces, lawn edges and openings to extend the living spaces.
04Parking and accessResolve vehicles, pedestrian entry and service movement early.
05Exterior designGive the house a proportioned facade with a coherent material palette.
06Construction drawingsCoordinate plans, sections, elevations and key architectural details.

Eight-step process

From brief to buildable drawings

Each stage closes the important decisions before the next one begins.

01

Brief and site analysis

Confirm the project brief, review the site and record the constraints that shape the design.

02

Concept planning

Test layout, zoning, access and movement before the architectural form is fixed.

03

Form and 3D studies

Develop the exterior character and review key views, proportions and materials.

04

Design development

Resolve dimensions, openings, levels, materials and the key technical decisions.

05

Working drawings

Prepare coordinated plans, sections, elevations and the agreed construction details.

06

Authority submission

Develop the required architectural set around the relevant approval process.

07

Structural coordination

Align spans, columns and stairs with the planned rooms and openings.

08

Final handover

Issue the agreed drawing package for pricing, coordination and construction.

Architecture fees

A clear range before the proposal

The fee covers architectural design and drawings. Construction, interior design and fit-out are separate unless they are added to the brief.

IncludedConcept plans, exterior 3D studies, design development and working drawings.
Final feeThe final proposal reflects floors, room requirements, drawing depth and authority submission needs.
Separate costsGovernment charges, surveys and third-party specialist fees are confirmed separately where needed.

items.q: How is a 10 Marla plan usually organized?
items.a: The layout normally separates formal guest areas from family living, bedrooms, kitchen and utility spaces.

items.q: Can you include a dirty kitchen or utility area?
items.a: Yes. Kitchen support, laundry and service access can be planned around the household brief.

items.q: Do you plan terraces and outdoor space?
items.a: Yes. Balconies, terraces and lawn connections are considered with privacy, sun and room layout.

items.q: Is structural coordination part of the service?
items.a: It is included in full architecture packages so the structural grid supports the approved plan.

items.q: Can Woodex prepare the submission set?
items.a: Yes. We can prepare and coordinate the required drawings for the relevant authority.
